announcer_mentions.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION (pre-read): no live series, no rules text. Outcome = whether a named word/phrase is uttered by broadcasters (which broadcast feed? national/home/away, which game). Chain: which broadcast crew assigned (national vs team feed) -> airtime/number of innings aired and delay/rain -> topic generation (storylines, player milestones, weather, stadium, pitcher events, prior-use word frequency per announcer) -> base rate of word per announcer per game from transcripts -> game-script events making word relevant (home runs, extras) -> resolution source (who decides, transcript/audio, homophones/plurals/compounds). Required inputs: announcer crew identity and per-crew word history, transcripts/closed captions, broadcast feed definition, game length, storyline calendar, rules text. Hazards: feed ambiguity, transcript source, partial-word matching, game delay/postponement, no rules sampled. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: Record matches my chain (crew/feed, exposure time, per-crew word rate, triggers, counting rules) and correctly states NO_LIVE_SERIES with no rules text; it adds a useful dispersion/zero-inflation point. Weaknesses: the whole input list is analogy-built, one data source is doubtful, and settlement_contract is marked COVERED despite rules being unknown.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: required_data 'Broadcast transcripts' lists 'Closed caption scraping from MLB.TV or network streams' as access 'free_limited'. MLB.TV/network streams are DRM-protected, ToS-restricted and not known to expose caption text; no public caption/transcript feed is verified. mlb.word_rate_per_broadcast_hour (primary) and mlb.mention_text depend on it. The record's own ann_transcript_data says no corpus exists; the 'free_limited' label contradicts that and should be own_capture/unavailable_public until verified.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:ann_caption_source_unverified

findings.text: Nonlinearity 'P(word)=1-exp(-lambda t)' assumes Poisson while the same record argues clustering/overdispersion; state the dispersion-adjusted form (e.g. NB or mixture) so the saturating shape is not mis-specified for topical words.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: nonlinearity on broadcast_airtime_distribution restated as negative-binomial zero probability 1-E[(1+lambda t/phi)^(-phi)] with phi per word class instead of Poisson.

extras_and_delay.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: Extras = game tied after 9 (reg) -> P(tie after 9) from run distribution of 9 innings (approx total-runs distribution; score tie is a function of both teams' run rate and variance, ~ 9-10% sym) -> unlike Tango, extras only needs 9-inning tie. Inputs: team run-scoring/prevention distribution, starter/bullpen quality through 8-9, closer/leverage, lineup depth; pitcher availability; home team leading after 8 -> no bottom 9 (game ends, no extras); rules: Rule 'originally scheduled' postponement/suspended game handling; doubleheader 7-inning (seven inning DH rules historically 2020-2021, now back to 9; confirm) ; playoffs no ties; regular season 'Manfred runner' (ghost runner) increases extras scoring but does not change P(extras). Delay: rain delay/postponement from weather forecast, roof status, stadium, month, park; official postponement criteria. Need rules text for delay market (none sampled). Hazards: postponement and 'originally scheduled' resolution, suspended games, shortened 5-inning game. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: Record's regulation-tie/tie-mass framing and weather-delay chain match mine. Differences: (a) author's P(extras) formula omits the path where the visitors lead after the top of the 9th and the home team ties without winning; (b) walk-off rate stated as 40-45% contradicts the author's own measurement (P(home scores >=1 in a half-inning) ~ 27-30%); (c) both live contracts (KXMLBEXTRAS, KXMLBDELAY) have RULES_TEXT in evidence under other archetypes but this record cites none; (d) no starter/lineup news input.

findings.text: Mechanism error in mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution / stage s2: 'extras equal tie after top 9 times the probability the home team does not score the winning run' and measurement 'P(extras) = P(tie after top 9) x (1 - P(walk-off)) + P(tied after 8.5 ... as described)' (garbled, incomplete). Extras also occur when the visitors lead after the top of the 9th and the home team ties but does not take the lead in the bottom of the 9th (one-run-deficit equalisers), and the KXMLBEXTRAS text is 'If at least 1 extra inning is played', i.e. tied after 9 complete innings. The input as specified would understate P(extras); define P(extras)=P(score level after 9 full innings) from the inning-by-inning joint chain, not a single conditional.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct; rewrote mlb.tie_entering_ninth_resolution measurement and stage s2 so P(extras)=P(level after nine complete innings) via inning-by-inning chain incl. visitor-lead-then-home-ties route and walk-off stopping rule.

findings.text: Archetype/series mis-mapping: live_series is empty here; KXMLBEXTRAS (RULES_TEXT: 'If at least 1 extra inning is played in the Milwaukee vs Tampa Bay ... game originally scheduled for Oct 28, 2026') sits in first_inning_and_inning_markets and KXMLBDELAY (RULES_TEXT, 'officially delayed due to weather ... delayed start time as well as any suspension or stoppage') in offfield_markets. The record sets rules_verification NO_LIVE_SERIES and rules_evidence [] even though it paraphrases both texts; the paraphrase is accurate but unquoted and uncheckable by the validator. Re-key the ledger or cite the sibling quotes.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added contract.series_mapping_issues for KXMLBEXTRAS and KXMLBDELAY (belong_in extras_and_delay) and quoted both rules texts verbatim in settlement_definition; rules_verification stays NO_LIVE_SERIES because the ledger files them elsewhere.

findings.text: Walk-off figure inconsistent: distribution says 'Conditional probability of walk-off about 40-45% when tied entering the bottom of the ninth' but the measurement defines it as P(home scores >=1 in the half-inning), which is roughly 27-30% against a typical reliever (league ~0.27 P(run) per half-inning). The 40-45% looks wrong; unverified.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct; stage s2 distribution changed from 40-45% to about 27-32% (P(home scores>=1) in a tied bottom 9, league P(run) per half-inning about 0.27), consistent with the measurement definition.

findings.text: category_coverage.availability_news NOT_APPLICABLE ('moves extras probability only through the run distribution') is circular: mlb.run_dist depends on the confirmed starters/lineups, yet no probable-pitcher/lineup/scratch input is listed for either extras or delay (roof decision and postponement news are also availability-type). Should be COVERED or GAP.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: availability_news changed from NOT_APPLICABLE to COVERED by sp_quality, roof_state and forecast_precip_timing, with new unresolved item ext_lineup_vintage for the card/probable-pitcher timestamp.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: mlb.lightning_proximity_exposure and the nonlinearity 'any strike within 8 miles triggers a 30-minute hold' present an 8-mile/30-minute rule as the league's policy; MLB publishes no uniform rule (stadium/umpire discretion; 8 mi and 30 min are common convention). GOES-R GLM gives optical flashes, not NLDN strikes, so the archive-based frequency is a proxy. Label as assumption.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: lightning measurement and nonlinearity now labelled as assumed convention (8 mi, 30 min not a uniform MLB rule) and GLM flagged as an optical-flash proxy for NLDN strikes.

first5_markets.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: F5 total/spread/winner/tie: starters' run prevention through ~5 innings (but starter may be pulled early: opener, injury, short-leash) -> times through order penalty -> bullpen enters when starter exits before 5 -> lineup quality vs handedness -> park/weather/umpire zone -> run-scoring distribution over 5 innings (negative binomial, correlated innings) -> discreteness: tie possibility, half-run strikes -> settlement: 5 innings completed (home leading after 4.5? if home leads after top of 5, bottom 5 may not be needed -> game official after 5 only if called). Rules: F5 market text says postponed->market remains open. If game is called before 5 complete? not stated. Inputs: probable pitchers, confirmed lineups, park, weather(wind/temp), umpire, bullpen workload, pitcher innings expectation, team offense vs hand, defense. Hazards: shortened game before 5 innings, suspended game, doubleheaders, tie strike structure, evidence pack puts F5 series in first_inning archetype not in first5 archetype (live_series empty). || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: Record's stage chain (starter identity/change risk, trips through order, slot exposure, early-exit mixture, environment, discrete tie mass) matches my derivation; its rules paraphrase (Tie strike, 'postponed or delayed ... remain open ... within two days') is accurate against KXMLBF5/F5SPREAD/F5TOTAL text. Differences: the live series are filed under the inning archetype so this record has no verifiable quotes; a measurement vector is internally inconsistent; a duplicate input is used in an interaction.

findings.text: Archetype/series mis-mapping: live_series is empty; KXMLBF5, KXMLBF5SPREAD, KXMLBF5TOTAL (all RULES_TEXT) are filed under first_inning_and_inning_markets. rules_verification is NO_LIVE_SERIES and rules_evidence is empty although the settlement text is paraphrased from those siblings. Consequence: the inputs here (f5_starter_change_risk, f5_lineup_slot_exposure, leash/tto) are not attached to the live contracts, while the inning archetype that holds them lacks these inputs (see first_inning finding). Needs re-keying or explicit cross-reference.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: contract.series_mapping_issues lists KXMLBF5, KXMLBF5SPREAD, KXMLBF5TOTAL, KXMLBF3, KXMLBF7 as belonging in first5_markets; rules_verification stays NO_LIVE_SERIES and verbatim KXMLBF5 text is cited in settlement_definition, claims marked conditional.

Per-slot weights must sum to the PA total.

first_inning_and_inning_markets.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: RFI/YRFI: P(at least 1 run in 1st, either team) = 1 - P(no run top)*P(no run bottom). Each half-inning: top 3 hitters (leadoff, 2,3) vs starter first inning (starters' first-inning ERA higher than average due to top of lineup guaranteed PAs 1-3 + 4.. ; first inning runs rate ~ 0.5/inning vs 0.45 avg). Inputs: starter first-inning splits (small sample -> shrink), lineup top-3 identities and OBP/power, handedness, park, weather, umpire, opener. Inning N total (9th inning specifically): game state: leverage, closer, home-not-batting (rules: 9th runs count even if home doesn't bat), game called early -> 'Fair Price'; inning-win tie (no runs by either = TIE) - the 'neither scores more runs' means scoreless OR equal runs. KXMLBWSTREAK = longest regular season win streak: season futures (mis-mapped here); KXMLBF3/F5/F7 winner/tie: line-score ties after N innings; F5 spread/total are first5_markets not this. Extras zombie-runner. Required: bullpen state in late innings, batting order position due up, pinch hitter, intentional walks, home-team skip. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: My chain: RFI as union of two top-of-order half-inning events; single-inning markets as half-inning run PMFs with leverage-chosen reliever and the home-skip rule; F3/F5/F7 as cumulative scores driven by starter exit; extras and win-streak as different objects. The record matches for RFI and the 9th inning but (a) omits the walk-off stopping rule in bottom-9 inning markets, (b) holds F3/F5/F7 live series without the starter-exit/slot/starter-change inputs that exist only in the first5 record, (c) adds a season-streak input to an inning archetype.

findings.text: Missing settlement hazard for KXMLBINNINGTOTAL/KXMLBINNINGWIN: in the bottom of the 9th (or any inning N>=9) the half-inning ends the moment the home team takes the lead, so home runs in that inning are truncated by the walk-off rule (a tied/one-run-behind home team can score at most the winning run(s) needed, outs not exhausted). mlb.ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher models only 'P(home bats)' and the pitcher; the 'Output: expected runs in top-9 and bottom-9' ignores the stopping rule, which biases over 1.5 runs and the Tie strike. The rules text counts runs 'in the 9th inning ... even if the home team does not bat' but is silent on truncation, so this is a distinct non-linearity that must be an input/stage.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct; walk-off stopping rule added to ninth_inning_entry_and_pitcher measurement, stage s4 text, a new absorbing-truncation nonlinearity and a conditional interaction replacing the old shrinkage one.

findings.text: Mis-filing leaves F3/F5/F7 live series (KXMLBF3, KXMLBF5, KXMLBF5SPREAD, KXMLBF5TOTAL, KXMLBF7: 5 of 10 series) without the inputs they need: stage s4 gives them only mlb.run_dist, mlb.tto, mlb.bullpen. Starter-exit hazard, starter-change risk and slot-weighted five-inning exposure (f5_starter_change_risk, f5_lineup_slot_exposure, f5_reliever_innings_share) exist only in first5_markets. The inning archetype's input list cannot be relied upon for these contracts.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: contract.series_mapping_issues routes KXMLBF3/F5/F5SPREAD/F5TOTAL/F7 to first5_markets; stage s4 now states those inputs are defined there and not claimed here; re-keying the ledger itself is outside this assignment.

The record itself says 'not inning markets'. It adds a required dataset ('Team game logs and schedule' feeding mlb.lineup_pit and the streak input; lineup_pit is not derived from schedule logs) and distorts category coverage (situational_schedule_motivation 'COVERED' only by the streak input). Move to season_futures; remove from this archetype's required inputs.

findings.text: Interaction ['mlb.first_inning','mlb.first_inning_splits','mlb.first_inning_markov_run_prob'] 'diminishing-returns' is a shrinkage weighting rule, not an interaction of causal drivers; mlb.first_inning vs mlb.first_inning_splits (KEEP_SECONDARY vs WEAK, f3_split DUPLICATE) overlap heavily and mlb.babip_luck is kept in stage s2 though audited WEAK/meaningless at inning scale.

game_moneyline.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: Win prob = f(starting pitchers, lineup, bullpen, defense, park, weather, home field ~54%, travel/rest, umpire) -> run-scoring distributions for each team (correlated via park/weather) -> run differential distribution (spread strike 'more than N runs' includes extras scoring; margin in extras 1 typically because walk-off ends) -> regulation + extras/ghost runner -> postseason: series win; division futures; ties impossible. Rules: sampled rules are division winners (futures) and series spread (games). KXMLBGAME rules NOT sampled (title only) - cannot confirm tie/suspended/postponement. Run line wins margin: walk-offs truncate home margins (home team winning in bottom 9th by 1 only at most... walk-off margin can be >1 with grand slam). Division winners/series spread/series winner are season/series-level (different mechanism: schedule strength remaining, standings) - mis-mapped under game_moneyline; spring training game (KXMLBSTGAME) ill-defined (lineups of prospects, split squad), All-Star KS (ASGKS). Required: SP identity & quality, lineup, bullpen, park, weather, umpire, rest/travel, standings, injuries, plus series-level (rotation order, games remaining). || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: My chain: starters + lineups + bullpen + defense + park/weather/umpire + home field -> correlated run processes -> win prob and margin distribution with walk-off truncation, plus series/division as separate aggregation mechanisms. The record covers all of this, honestly marks KXMLBGAME as TITLE_ONLY, and flags misfiling. Differences: automatic-runner assumption in a postseason context, a mis-scaled constant in the day-specific lineup delta, and no regular-season standings/clinch motivation input.

findings.text: Archetype/series mis-mapping weakens the evidence: of 12 live series only KXMLBSPREAD (RULES_TEXT) is a single-game contract with text; KXMLBGAME itself, KXMLBSTGAME (spring training, where ties after extras are possible) and KXMLBASGKS are title-only, and 6 division-winner series plus KXMLBSERIES/KXMLBSERIESSPREAD are futures/series objects. rules_verification PARTIALLY_VERIFIED is honest, but extras/tie/void treatment for the core moneyline remains unverified, and stage s5 'Series and division aggregation' adds inputs (series_context, postseason_leverage_usage, series_game_state) that are not defined in new_inputs and are shared with other archetypes.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: partly correct; recorded 6 division futures to season_futures, KXMLBSERIES/SERIESSPREAD to a new playoff-series archetype, KXMLBASGKS to all_star_week_events; KXMLBGAME rules stay unverified (ml_gamewinner_rules). mlb.series_context, postseason_leverage_usage and series_game_state are existing catalog inputs, so the claim they are undefined is incorrect.

findings.text: Measurement error in mlb.lineup_strength_delta: 'scaling (about 1.15 runs per 0.100 wOBA per 38 PA team game )'. Converting wOBA to runs is runs = dwOBA/wOBA_scale (~1.2) x PA, i.e. ~3.2 runs per 0.100 team-wide wOBA over 38 PA; 1.15 looks like the wOBA scale used as a multiplier. PA_share vector already sums to 38.2 so the extra 'x 9 innings' is also double counting. Fix before use.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct; lineup_strength_delta now converts wOBA to runs by dividing by wOBA_scale (about 1.2; 0.100 over 38 PA is about 3.2 runs) with no extra 9-inning multiplier.

findings.text: Summary and stage s4 state that ties after nine 'resolve by an automatic-runner extra-inning game'. The sampled contracts are postseason (Championship Series, Oct 28); the automatic runner is, to my knowledge, a regular-season rule only (unverified here). Spread margins in extras and the walk-off truncation of margin depend on this.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: reviewer correct per my knowledge that the automatic runner is regular-season only; stage s4 text now says regular-season extras start with an automatic runner while the sampled postseason contracts, to my knowledge unverified for 2026, start extras with bases empty.

findings.text: No regular-season motivation/standings input (clinched/eliminated, resting regulars, September roster expansion, tanking) for KXMLBGAME; situational_schedule_motivation is COVERED only by rest_travel and series_context. Day-specific lineup_strength_delta partly captures resting, but starter handling and bullpen usage in meaningless games do not flow through it.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added new input mlb.regular_season_stakes_and_rest_policy (clinched/eliminated flags, rest-day probabilities, leash shift) in stage s1 and situational_schedule_motivation coverage, gated off for postseason games.

findings.text: mlb.opp_strength KEEP_SECONDARY is described as duplicating the opponent adjustment inside run-based talent; it should be audited DUPLICATE or folded. mlb.rest_travel is KEEP_CONTEXT yet it is the only schedule input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: opp_strength reason rewritten (redundant for single games, kept secondary only for team-level latent strength in series/division aggregation) and rest_travel reason updated now that a second schedule input exists.

findings.text: Series spread: 'wins by more than 3.5 games ... best-of-7' resolves only on a 4-0 sweep (margin 4); record says '4-0 sweep or equivalent'. Fine for best-of-7 but best-of-5/9 series (Division Series, other rounds) change the object; round format is not an input.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: added a variants_and_edge_cases entry that a 3.5-game spread resolves only on a 4-0 sweep in a best-of-7 and is unsatisfiable in a best-of-5, making round format a contract-level input; series spread mapped to a new playoff-series archetype.

game_total_and_team_total.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: Total runs = sum of two correlated team run counts: runs per team ~ overdispersed discrete (neg binomial/ compound); drivers: both SP quality, bullpens (innings 6-9), lineups, park run factor, weather (temp, wind direction/speed, humidity/air density, roof), umpire zone, game state (home skips bottom 9 when leading -> home team scores fewer opportunities; team total for home reduced), extras (ghost runner adds runs; extra innings only when tied), pace. Strikes: 'more 8.5' (typo) 'N+' team total ('scores 8+ runs'), floor 7.5. KXMLBSERIESGAMES = series length (best-of-7 number of games) is different mechanism: series win prob per game and who wins -> distribution of series length. Required: rest/bullpen usage, lineups, plate umpire, forecast, park factors. Hazards: postponed/suspended game, called game (rain) shortened -> total by rules? not sampled; home team not batting in 9th reduces. Team total also depends on whether the game is 7-inning DH. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: My chain: two correlated overdispersed team run counts driven by opposing starter/bullpen, lineup, park/weather/umpire, truncated by the home-skip and walk-off rules and extended by extras; series-games total as a separate series-length mechanism. The record matches and verbatim quotes check out, including the 'collectively score more 8.5' typo and the title/rule team-total mismatch. Differences: over-read ambiguity on strike wording, walk-off truncation missing, extras runs estimated under an automatic-runner assumption for postseason contracts.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED / mechanism: mlb.extras_run_contribution is measured 'with automatic runner ... 2020-2025 extras ... about 0.9-1.1 runs per half'. All sampled totals are postseason (Championship Series, Oct 28); to my knowledge the automatic runner is not used in MLB postseason games, in which case extras runs per half are much lower and the estimate (and its pre-extras tail contribution) is wrong for those contracts. Confirm rule scope before using; contract text is silent on whether extras count.
findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:tot_postseason_extras_rule

findings.text: Strike wording ambiguity is over-read: KXMLBTEAMTOTAL floor_strike 7.5 'greater' with rule '8+' and KXMLBTOTAL floor 8.5 'greater' ('more 8.5') are the same event (>=9 runs), a typographical omission rather than integer-versus-half-run ambiguity; tot_strike_wording should be downgraded. Real unresolved item is whether extras runs count.

'Expected truncation loss = P(skip) x ~0.5 runs' is applied to the game total but not separated for KXMLBTEAMTOTAL of the home team.
findings.resolution: RESOLVED: bottom_ninth_truncation measurement now includes walk-off truncation of the home half and applies it separately to the home team total versus the visitor total and game total.

findings.resolution: DEFERRED_TO_UNRESOLVED:tot_park_axis_source

hitter_hits_and_total_bases.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: Hits/TB/HRR = PA count (lineup slot, team offense, game length, home-skip-bottom-9, blowouts, pinch hit replacement) x per-PA outcome distribution (single/double/triple/HR/out/walk/HBP) conditioned on batter vs specific pitcher (handedness platoon), pitcher's quality, bullpen exposure after starter exits (times-through-order), park (hit/HR factor), weather, defense/BABIP luck, umpire. Quantity: hits ~ sum of Bernoulli PAs (~ binomial with n AB 3-5), TB heavy-tailed. HRR = hits+runs+RBI: correlated with teammates (lineup), runs depend on team scoring/ batting slot; RBI depends on runners on base from hitters ahead. Settlement per rules: scratched or not in starting lineup -> fair market price; starts but no PA -> fair price; pinch-hit entries don't count; settles if >=1 PA. Inputs: confirmed lineup & batting order, opposing starter + handedness, park/weather, hitter xStats/contact quality, platoon splits, speed (infield hits), bullpen. Hazards: lineup release timing (1-3 hours pre-game), late scratches, ASG/HR derby TITLE_ONLY mis-mapped (KXMLBHA, HRDERBYLONGEST), series-level. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: My chain: PA budget (slot, team scoring, game length, removal risk) x per-PA outcome mix (batter quality/contact, platoon vs starter then relievers, park/weather/defense, speed) with overlapping hits/TB/HRR ladders and the start-and-one-PA gate. Record matches closely; settlement quotes verified verbatim (scratch/non-starter/zero-PA = fair market price, pinch-hit at-bats excluded). Differences are minor input-hygiene issues.

findings.text: mlb.contact_dist is audited 'a modelling target, not information' yet verdict KEEP_SECONDARY and it appears as an input in the 'threshold' interaction ['mlb.expected_pa','mlb.late_replacement_risk','mlb.contact_dist']; a target is not an interaction input. Should be BENCHMARK_ONLY/WEAK and the interaction restated on PA-count x per-PA probability.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: required_data 'Weather and context' lists 'game total proxy (model)' feeding rbi_opportunity/run_scoring_opportunity. State that it comes from the project's own run model, not a sportsbook total or Kalshi total price; otherwise it is a market-derived input.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: Lineup-vintage risk is not in unresolved for this archetype: markets list before lineups post and the rules refund non-starters, so confirmed-lineup timestamps (own capture) are a hard requirement; only game_moneyline records it.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: KXMLBHRR combines H+R+RBI but only slot-level rbi_opportunity/run_scoring_opportunity inputs exist; there is no lineup-neighbour on-base chain here (it exists in the rbis archetype as mlb.pa_base_out_state_chain), so the runs/RBI components of the live HRR series are modelled more crudely than the same events in the RBI archetype.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: The ledger files KXMLBHA (hits allowed), KXMLBASGHIT and KXMLBHRDERBYLONGEST here (title-only); disclosed, but the 'hits_misfiled_series' entry does not note that hits-allowed is a pitcher market needing none of these hitter inputs.
findings.resolution: OPEN

hitter_home_runs.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: HR ~ PA x P(HR per PA) with P = f(batter power (barrel%, exit velo, launch angle, pull air), pitcher HR-suppression (HR/FB, hard hit allowed, pitch mix), park HR factor by handedness (pull side distance), wind/temp/air density/roof, platoon). Rare event ~ 0.5 per PA 3-4.5% -> game prob ~ 12-20%; discrete, binary N+ rung; overdispersion small. Bullpen exposure. Settlement: same player participation rules as hits (starter with >=1 PA). Series HR (KXMLBSERIESHR) counts total across series incl extras: depends on # games played & his playing time per game, rest days, injury; KXMLBWALKOFFS = playoff team-level walk-off count (a different object: count of home-walk-off games in playoffs; depends on # playoff games, tied-late-game rate, home team batting last) mis-mapped as hitter archetype; HR derby series (title-only) = event of different mechanism (pitch by BP pitchers, 3-min rounds, bonus time, fatigue); season HR totals; AS game HR. Required: lineup confirmed, SP, park, weather, bats metrics. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: My chain: PA budget x per-PA HR probability (batter power/pull-air, pitcher HR vulnerability by hand, park/wind/air-density carry) as a Poisson-binomial with shared game environment; series HR as exposure aggregation; walk-off count and derby as separate mechanisms. Record covers the single-game and series HR well, with accurate quotes. Differences: KXMLBWALKOFFS (a RULES_TEXT live series) gets no inputs at all, plus some unverified fields and unmodelled starter-change risk.

findings.text: KXMLBWALKOFFS (RULES_TEXT: 'at least 5 walk-offs in the 2026 Pro Baseball Playoffs') is a team/league count of home-team game-ending events, not a hitter HR. The record admits it is 'a team-level binomial over games' in s5 but defines no input for it (number of remaining playoff games, rate of games reaching the bottom of the 9th tied or home-trailing by <=3, closer/bullpen quality, extras probability, home-team share). No new_inputs, interaction or required_data covers it, and it is not in unresolved. A live-series family with no required inputs is an undisclosed gap; it belongs with game_total/extras or season counting specials.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: required_data lists Statcast fields 'bat_speed, swing_length, squared_up' as event-level columns. bat_speed/swing_length appear in Statcast search exports (2023+/2024), but 'squared_up' is, to my knowledge, a leaderboard metric, not a per-event CSV column; mlb.bat_tracking (secondary) may need to be derived.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: KXMLBSERIESHR is described as 'no start gate' because the text is silent; the text does not say how a series player who is injured or does not play is settled (No versus refund). Record asserts 'a hitter who misses a game simply has fewer PAs' as settlement fact; it is an inference and should be CONTRACT_AMBIGUOUS.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: Opposing-starter change before first pitch is not modelled for the single-game HR ladder even though the contract is only conditional on the hitter (a pitcher scratch does not refund); lineup_pit is the only availability input and a starter-change risk input (as in first5) is absent. mlb.platoon is KEEP_SECONDARY while described as 'superseded' by hand-specific profiles; mlb.pa_sim is a method, not an input, yet appears in stage s5 and coverage.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: game_shared_hr_dispersion is stated to be estimated from 'team-plus-opponent HR counts versus the Poisson-binomial expectation given the matchup model'; this requires the project's own matchup model to exist first (circular for a pregame requirement) and has no pre-registered feature fallback.
findings.resolution: OPEN

hitter_rbis_runs_sb.rederivation_notes: OWN DERIVATION: RBI = opportunities (runners on base when batter up; lineup slot, hitters ahead's OBP) x conversion (hits/sac fly/ HR which drives himself and runners; ground-out RBI; walks with bases loaded) -> strongly team-run dependent and lineup-slot dependent; discrete heavy-tail; correlated with teammates; Runs scored = batter's own on-base prob x probability of being driven in/ HR; SB = attempts (speed, catcher pop time, pitcher time-to-plate, hold runners, lefty pickoff, score context) x success. Settlement same participation rule (>=1 PA) - verified for RBI only; runs/SB: no live series sampled (only KXMLBRBI) so settlement for runs/SB unverified; HRR is in other archetype. Required: batting slot, confirmed lineup, teammates' OBP ahead, opposing pitcher/bullpen, park, game total environment, catcher/pitcher SB defense. || DIFFERENCES AFTER READING RECORD: My chain: RBI = PAs x runners-on-base distribution (hitters ahead, opposing pitcher/team scoring) x conversion by base-out state with GIDP exclusion; SB = reaching first with second open x green-light decision x success vs pitcher hold/catcher arm; runs scored via on-base x being driven in. Record matches and is honest that only KXMLBRBI is filed (verified text) while KXMLBSB sits in counting specials and runs has no series. Differences: some settlement/rules claims not in the text, and unverified battery data fields.

findings.text: SOURCE_UNVERIFIED: required_data 'Steal opportunity log with battery data' claims Baseball Savant provides pop time, pitcher time_to_plate and sprint speed 'Season leaderboards and per-play' as access free. Savant publishes catcher pop time and a pitcher running-game leaderboard and sprint speed, but a pitcher time-to-plate field and per-play pop time are not confirmed (a web check found no time-to-plate definition). mlb.sb_context (KEEP_PRIMARY) and the 'convex combined hold time + pop time ~3.3 s' nonlinearity depend on them; proxies (pickoff/lead data, season pop time) would change the required data.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: VAR 'a run scoring on a ground-ball double play, an error, or catcher interference is not an RBI' is background, not rules text, and partly inaccurate: official scoring credits an RBI when catcher interference/obstruction or a walk/HBP forces in a run, and may credit an RBI on an error if the scorer judges the run would score anyway. Mark as official-scoring assumption; the Kalshi text only says 'RBIs recorded'.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: Stolen-base settlement rests on a sibling: KXMLBSB (RULES_TEXT, same Player Participation criteria, '1+ stolen bases') is filed under unreg:player_and_team_counting_specials, yet the SB mechanism (stage s4, sb_context, sb_opportunity_conversion, baserunning, rule_regime, team_style) is built here with no quote. Cite the KXMLBSB text or re-key; also KXMLBHRR (runs/RBI component) is filed under the hits archetype.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: Quantitative claims stated as fact without source: 'attempt hazard jumps above about 28 ft/s sprint speed' and 'time to plate plus pop time exceeds roughly 3.3 sec'; interaction ['mlb.expected_pa','mlb.park','mlb.sp_quality'] 'threshold' is a convexity in run environment, not a threshold, and uses no game-total-environment input.
findings.resolution: OPEN

findings.text: rbi_opportunity_vintage notes lineup vintage but not the on-deck/batting-behind effect: intentional-walk and pitch-around behaviour depends on the next hitter and is a conditional input stated only in an interaction (no measurable input for batting-behind quality).
